import type { AngleMode } from "../api/types";
import CalcButton from "./CalcButton";

/**
 * Props for {@link AngleModeToggle}.
 *
 * Presentational component: the Calculator container (task 35.3) owns the
 * `angleMode` state and the flip logic. This control only DISPLAYS the active
 * mode (Requirement 22.6) and calls `onToggle` on activation to request a flip
 * (Requirement 22.7).
 */
export interface AngleModeToggleProps {
  /** The currently active angle unit for trigonometric evaluation. */
  angleMode: AngleMode;
  /**
   * Requests a flip to the other angle mode. The container flips the mode in
   * React state; that update is synchronous on click and re-renders immediately,
   * well within the 100 ms update budget (Requirement 22.7), so simply invoking
   * this callback satisfies the timing requirement.
   */
  onToggle: () => void;
}

/**
 * A toggle control that displays the active angle mode and flips it on
 * activation.
 *
 * - Displays the active mode as a short visible label — `RAD` for radians,
 *   `DEG` for degrees (Requirement 22.6).
 * - On activation it calls {@link AngleModeToggleProps.onToggle}; the container
 *   updates state immediately, so the displayed mode updates within 100 ms
 *   (Requirement 22.7).
 * - Reuses the Stage 1 {@link CalcButton} accessibility pattern (native
 *   `<button>`, visible label + matching `aria-label`, inherited focus/pressed
 *   state). The accessible name communicates both the current mode and that
 *   activating switches it (e.g. "Angle mode: radians. Activate to switch to
 *   degrees."). Uses the `action` variant.
 */
export function AngleModeToggle({ angleMode, onToggle }: AngleModeToggleProps) {
  const isRadians = angleMode === "radians";
  const label = isRadians ? "RAD" : "DEG";
  const otherMode = isRadians ? "degrees" : "radians";
  const ariaLabel = `Angle mode: ${angleMode}. Activate to switch to ${otherMode}.`;

  return (
    <CalcButton
      label={label}
      ariaLabel={ariaLabel}
      onActivate={onToggle}
      variant="action"
      className="angle-mode-toggle"
    />
  );
}

export default AngleModeToggle;

import "./CalcButton.css";

/**
 * Semantic grouping for a calculator control, used to hook variant-specific
 * styling (e.g., color-coding operators vs. digits). Styling itself is the
 * responsibility of the theme task; this component only exposes the class hook.
 */
export type CalcButtonVariant = "digit" | "operator" | "action";

/**
 * Props for {@link CalcButton}.
 *
 * The component renders a native `<button>`, so keyboard operability and the
 * implicit `role="button"` are inherent (Requirement 12.2 — no explicit role is
 * needed on a native button). Focus is never suppressed.
 */
export interface CalcButtonProps {
  /**
   * Visible text identifying the button's function, e.g. `"7"`, `"+"`, `"="`.
   * Rendered inside the button so every control carries a visible label
   * (Requirement 11.6).
   */
  label: string;
  /**
   * Accessible label describing the button's function in words (e.g. `"plus"`,
   * `"divide"`, `"equals"`, `"clear"`) rather than only the symbol. It must
   * correspond to the visible function (Requirement 12.1). When omitted, it
   * falls back to {@link CalcButtonProps.label} so the accessible name always
   * matches the visible label.
   */
  ariaLabel?: string;
  /** Invoked when the button is activated by click, touch, or keyboard. */
  onActivate: () => void;
  /** Optional additional class names appended to the button's class list. */
  className?: string;
  /** Semantic grouping used as a styling hook. Defaults to `"digit"`. */
  variant?: CalcButtonVariant;
}

/**
 * A single calculator key rendered as a native `<button>`.
 *
 * - Shows a visible label identifying its function (Requirement 11.6).
 * - Exposes an `aria-label` matching that function, describing it in words
 *   (Requirement 12.1); as a native button its `role="button"` is implicit
 *   (Requirement 12.2).
 * - Indicates its pressed/active state visually. The active-state indication is
 *   driven by CSS `:active` / `:focus-visible` hooks in `CalcButton.css`
 *   (Requirement 11.5); focus is left intact for keyboard operation.
 */
export function CalcButton({
  label,
  ariaLabel,
  onActivate,
  className,
  variant = "digit",
}: CalcButtonProps) {
  const classes = ["calc-button", `calc-button--${variant}`];
  if (className) {
    classes.push(className);
  }

  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      className={classes.join(" ")}
      aria-label={ariaLabel ?? label}
      onClick={onActivate}
    >
      {label}
    </button>
  );
}

export default CalcButton;

/**
 * Pure state management for the calculator's RPN (Reverse Polish Notation) mode.
 *
 * This reducer owns ONLY the Frontend_Client's RPN input and Stack_Display state:
 * the active mode (Standard vs RPN), the in-progress operand entry, the X/Y/Z/T
 * operand stack, and an RPN error indication. Like the Stage 1/2 calculator
 * reducer, it NEVER computes any arithmetic result of an Expression — every result
 * is produced by the Backend_Service via the Evaluate_Endpoint (Requirement 39.9).
 * The reducer's job is limited to editing the operand entry and recording the
 * confirmed backend-driven stack / errors.
 *
 * Result and error are mutually exclusive: a confirmed stack update clears any
 * error, and an error leaves the stack unchanged and shows no computed result
 * (Requirements 39.7, 40.7).
 *
 * Requirements: 39.1, 39.2, 39.4, 39.6, 39.9, 40.2, 40.7
 */

/**
 * The calculator operating mode.
 * - `'standard'`: the unchanged Stage 1/2 infix workflow (default, Requirement 39.1).
 * - `'rpn'`: the postfix / stack workflow with an X/Y/Z/T Stack_Display.
 */
export type Mode = 'standard' | 'rpn';

/**
 * The four visible levels of the RPN operand stack, bottom-visible-first.
 *
 * Each level holds a Decimal operand **string** (never a `number`) so exact
 * precision carries through from the backend without float coercion. A level is
 * `undefined` when the stack does not currently hold a value at that position
 * (Requirements 40.1, 40.6).
 */
export interface StackLevels {
  x?: string;
  y?: string;
  z?: string;
  t?: string;
}

/**
 * The complete RPN UI state owned by the reducer.
 *
 * - `mode`: the active calculator mode. Defaults to `'standard'` so RPN state is
 *   fully isolated until the user opts in (Requirement 39.1).
 * - `operandEntry`: the in-progress operand string being typed before it is pushed
 *   onto the stack. Empty (`''`) when no operand is being entered.
 * - `stack`: the X/Y/Z/T operand stack of Decimal strings (Requirement 40.1).
 * - `error`: the RPN error indication, or `null` when none is displayed. The
 *   reducer never holds a locally computed result, so `error` is mutually exclusive
 *   with any backend-confirmed stack update (Requirements 39.7, 40.7).
 */
export interface RpnState {
  mode: Mode;
  operandEntry: string;
  stack: StackLevels;
  error: string | null;
}

/**
 * The initial, empty state: Standard_Mode, no operand entry, an empty stack, and no
 * error (Requirement 39.1).
 */
export const initialRpnState: RpnState = {
  mode: 'standard',
  operandEntry: '',
  stack: {},
  error: null,
};

/**
 * The set of actions the RPN UI can dispatch.
 *
 * String literal `type` discriminants form a discriminated union so the reducer can
 * exhaustively narrow each case with no use of `any`.
 */
export type RpnAction =
  /** Switch mode, clearing the operand entry, stack, and error (Requirement 39.2). */
  | { type: 'TOGGLE_MODE' }
  /** Append a single character to the in-progress operand entry. */
  | { type: 'APPEND_OPERAND_CHAR'; char: string }
  /** Enter_Control: push the operand entry onto the stack (Requirements 39.4, 40.2). */
  | { type: 'PUSH' }
  /** Replace the stack from a confirmed backend success, clearing any error (Requirement 40.3). */
  | { type: 'SET_STACK'; stack: StackLevels }
  /** Record an RPN error, leaving the stack unchanged (Requirements 39.6, 39.7, 40.7). */
  | { type: 'SET_RPN_ERROR'; error: string }
  /** Reset to the initial empty state, preserving the current mode. */
  | { type: 'RESET' };

/**
 * Compile-time exhaustiveness guard. If a new {@link RpnAction} variant is added
 * without a matching `case`, the `never`-typed parameter fails to type-check,
 * flagging the missing branch. At runtime an unhandled action leaves state unchanged.
 */
function assertNever(_action: never, state: RpnState): RpnState {
  return state;
}

/**
 * Pure reducer computing the next {@link RpnState} from the current state and an
 * action. It performs no side effects and no arithmetic (Requirement 39.9).
 */
export function rpnReducer(state: RpnState, action: RpnAction): RpnState {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'TOGGLE_MODE':
      // Switching mode clears the operand entry, the stack, and the result/error so
      // no value carries across the switch (Requirement 39.2).
      return {
        mode: state.mode === 'standard' ? 'rpn' : 'standard',
        operandEntry: '',
        stack: {},
        error: null,
      };

    case 'APPEND_OPERAND_CHAR':
      // Build up the in-progress operand one character at a time. Any prior error
      // indication is cleared as the user resumes entering input.
      return {
        ...state,
        operandEntry: state.operandEntry + action.char,
        error: null,
      };

    case 'PUSH':
      // Enter_Control. With an empty operand entry this is a no-op that surfaces an
      // error indication rather than pushing nothing (Requirement 39.6).
      if (state.operandEntry.length === 0) {
        return {
          ...state,
          error: 'no operand to push',
        };
      }
      // With a non-empty operand entry, place it at X and shift X->Y->Z->T, dropping
      // the previous T when the stack is full; then clear the operand entry
      // (Requirements 39.4, 40.2).
      return {
        ...state,
        operandEntry: '',
        error: null,
        stack: {
          x: state.operandEntry,
          y: state.stack.x,
          z: state.stack.y,
          t: state.stack.z,
        },
      };

    case 'SET_STACK':
      // A confirmed backend success replaces the stack with the new levels and
      // clears any error, keeping result and error mutually exclusive
      // (Requirements 40.3, 39.7).
      return {
        ...state,
        stack: action.stack,
        error: null,
      };

    case 'SET_RPN_ERROR':
      // A guard rejection, backend Error_Response, or transport failure records an
      // error indication, leaves the stack unchanged, and shows no computed result
      // (Requirements 39.6, 39.7, 40.7).
      return {
        ...state,
        error: action.error,
      };

    case 'RESET':
      // Reset clears the operand entry, stack, and error but preserves the current
      // mode so a reset within RPN_Mode stays in RPN_Mode.
      return {
        ...initialRpnState,
        mode: state.mode,
      };

    default: {
      // Exhaustiveness guard: if a new action type is added without a matching case,
      // this assignment fails to type-check. Unknown actions leave state unchanged.
      return assertNever(action, state);
    }
  }
}

/*
 * HistoryPanel.css — responsive, accessible layout for the History_Panel
 * (Task 36; Requirements 21.2-21.8, 22.3, 22.4, 22.5, 22.9, 11.1-11.4).
 *
 * The panel re-flows with no horizontal overflow or clipping across all three
 * breakpoints: long expressions/results wrap (overflow-wrap) instead of pushing
 * the width, and a long list scrolls VERTICALLY inside a capped-height region
 * rather than overflowing horizontally (Req 22.3, 22.4, 22.9). Entry controls
 * are `.calc-button`s, so the >=44px touch target and the focus/pressed
 * indicators are inherited from CalcButton.css (Req 22.5, 11.4). The Clear
 * button mirrors the same `.calc-button` chrome.
 *
 * Contrast: the title uses `--color-scientific-heading` -> 10.67:1 on the panel
 * bg (Req 11.1/11.2); the empty-state text uses `--color-muted` (>7:1); the
 * panel boundary uses `--color-scientific-border` -> 5.30:1 (Req 11.3).
 */

.history-panel {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--gap, 0.5rem);
  width: 100%;
  min-width: 0;
  /* A light divider separates the history region from the keypads above
     without pushing width; boundary >= 3:1 on the panel bg (Req 11.3). */
  border-top: 1px solid var(--color-scientific-border, #7c8ab5);
  padding-top: var(--gap, 0.5rem);
}

.history-panel__header {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--gap, 0.5rem);
  flex-wrap: wrap;
}

.history-panel__title {
  margin: 0;
  /* Large/bold heading text: 10.67:1 on the panel bg (Req 11.1/11.2). */
  color: var(--color-scientific-heading, #cdd6ea);
  font-size: 1rem;
}

/* The Clear control is a `.calc-button`; reaffirm the 44px touch floor so it
   stays tappable at mobile widths even with its short "Clear" label (Req 22.5). */
.history-panel__clear {
  min-height: var(--touch-min, 44px);
  min-width: var(--touch-min, 44px);
}

/* Empty-state message shown when there are no entries (Requirement 21.8). */
.history-panel__empty {
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--color-muted, #c3ccdf); /* secondary text, > 7:1 (Req 11.1) */
}

/* Newest-first list of entries (Requirement 21.2). A long history scrolls
   vertically inside a capped-height region so it never overflows horizontally
   and never pushes the panel taller than the viewport (Req 22.3, 22.9). */
.history-panel__list {
  list-style: none;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--gap, 0.5rem);
  min-width: 0;
  max-height: clamp(10rem, 40vh, 22rem);
  overflow-y: auto;
  /* Keep the vertical scrollbar from overlapping the right-aligned text. */
  overflow-x: hidden;
}

/*
 * Each entry exposes two independently selectable controls: the expression and
 * the result (Requirements 21.3, 21.4). They stack within the row and each
 * fills the available width so both are comfortable touch targets.
 */
.history-panel__item {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: calc(var(--gap, 0.5rem) / 2);
  min-width: 0;
}

/*
 * Long expressions/results wrap instead of forcing the panel wider (Req 22.3);
 * the button text can span multiple lines, so allow auto height while keeping
 * the inherited 44px minimum (Req 22.5). `height: auto` lets a wrapped,
 * multi-line label grow downward rather than clip (Req 22.4).
 */
.history-panel__expression,
.history-panel__result {
  width: 100%;
  min-width: 0;
  height: auto;
  min-height: var(--touch-min, 44px);
  text-align: right;
  white-space: normal;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  word-break: break-word;
}

/* =========================================================================
 * Responsive re-flow (Req 22.3, 22.4, 22.9)
 * On wider viewports the two entry controls sit side by side (expression | =
 * result) to use the extra width, still wrapping long content and never
 * overflowing horizontally.
 * ========================================================================= */
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .history-panel__item {
    flex-direction: row;
    align-items: stretch;
  }

  .history-panel__expression {
    flex: 1 1 60%;
  }

  .history-panel__result {
    flex: 1 1 40%;
  }

  /* A little more room for the list on taller tablet/desktop layouts. */
  .history-panel__list {
    max-height: clamp(12rem, 45vh, 28rem);
  }
}
